source.title: Evaluating PhaseNet on Teleseismic Data with MsPASS
source.authors: Jinxing Ma; Yinzhi Wang; G. Pavlis; Chenbo Yin

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses language-model scaling laws as motivation, but its seismic-picker results do not measure held-out language-model loss, fit a power law, or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation. Its PhaseNet size comparison reports different metrics and does not test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper benchmarks PhaseNet size against seismic picking accuracy, training loss, and inference throughput. These are related scaling results, but they do not measure the losses or trends specified by the claim versions. The reported size-comparison results are recorded as findings that fit no version. The PhaseNet-NCEDC domain-shift comparison and residual-histogram descriptions are left out because they are not size-scaling results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. (2020) only as motivation. It compares just two PhaseNet sizes (0.268M vs 32.392M) on seismic picking metrics, training loss and throughput. It fits no power law, measures no held-out loss trend, and checks no extrapolation or allocation. Two points cannot show whether a power-law form holds in this domain, so V5 is not tested either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude explicitly that scaling PhaseNet is more practical on GPUs than on CPUs, and that the accuracy gain is not proportional to the efficiency loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales convolutional channel capacity in a seismic phase picker and evaluates picking metrics and throughput; it does not use or fit the language-model scaling-law recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported throughput cost differs by hardware: the larger model reduces throughput by 87.2% on the GPU and 97.3% on the CPU.

fits_no_version.finding: On the held-out USArray teleseismic test set, a roughly 120-fold parameter increase (filter factor 1→8) raised precision by 15.6%, recall by 23.2% and F1 by 19.4%, and gave 25.3% more picks within ±0.1 s. It cut inference throughput by 87.2% on an A100 GPU and by 97.3% on a 128-core CPU node.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For PhaseNet seismic phase picking, a roughly 120-fold increase in parameters gives modest accuracy gains at a large inference-throughput cost, and the cost is larger on CPUs than on GPUs.

fits_no_version.finding: Both models reached training loss below 0.05 early: the larger model within 10 epochs, the standard model within 25. The larger model reached a slightly lower minimum training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this setup, the larger PhaseNet converges faster and reaches a slightly lower training loss.

record.problems: The scaling comparison has only two model sizes and reports seismic picking metrics and training loss rather than held-out language-model loss or fitted power laws. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the compared results.
record.rows_left_out: The PhaseNet-NCEDC versus PhaseNet-USArray domain-shift metrics and Figure 3 residual-histogram results were not included because they do not compare model sizes; see Table 2 and Figure 3.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; any power-law fit.
Extrapolating fitted laws from small runs to much larger runs.
Effect of shape at fixed parameter count. Only channel width is changed, and that changes the parameter count.
Power-law form in another modality. Only two model sizes are compared, no loss-versus-size curve is fitted, and dev/test loss is not reported by size.
Downstream performance predicted from scale or loss. The two-point accuracy gain is not tied to a scaling law.
Dependence of exponents or allocations on fitting choices; bending away from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to no version. The only engagement with scaling laws is in the introduction: one sentence citing Kaplan, and a remark that scaling laws depend on architecture, data and task. The study reports no evidence on that remark. Dev loss was used for early stopping but is not reported by model size.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fitting and several orders of magnitude.
Fitting laws on small language-model runs and predicting much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their growth with compute.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the paper compares only two PhaseNet sizes and does not fit such a law.
Downstream language-task performance versus scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.
